* fix: read back a saved MCP result whose notice gives a line count (#401)

Claude Code 2.1.305 words the saved-result notice "result (67,095
characters across 28 lines) exceeds maximum allowed tokens". The reader
added for #391 matched only "result (N characters)", so on current Claude
Code it stored the notice instead of the result: #391 again, in a fix
that has not shipped yet.

The count may now carry " across N lines"; when it does, the saved file
must have that many lines as well as the stated characters. Run end to
end on the live notice and file: 65.5 KB stored and summarized to 4.3 KB,
where the notice alone was 1.4 KB.

* fix: accept either line count for a saved file that ends in a newline

Review on #402: the line check counted split("\n") segments, so a saved
file ending in a newline has one more segment than lines. How Claude
Code counts that case is not known, so both readings are accepted; the
exact character count already rules out a different file.","tree":{"sha":"16a73bfbd6beb9a743c121208b1dfc25fc69d4f5","url":"https://api.github.com/repos/sakebomb/mcp-recall/git/trees/16a73bfbd6beb9a743c121208b1dfc25fc69d4f5"},"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/sakebomb/mcp-recall/git/commits/e672ecb45167a1629ccabd602ccbacea1c6e11ac","comment_count":0,"verification":{"verified":true,"reason":"valid","signature":"-----BEGIN PGP SIGNATURE-----

each diagnostic of ruff's default full output format (#399)

* fix: keep each diagnostic of ruff's default full output format (#397)

Ruff's default format prints the rule code and message on one line and
the location on a " --> " line under it. The compiler handler parsed only
the one-line path:line:col form, so the code line matched nothing, the

A public quality claim needs evidence a skeptic can rerun. bench checks
hand-picked facts on hand-written fixtures; fidelity runs on private
transcripts. Neither can be published as proof.

bun run quality runs each case in benchmark/corpus/ through four arms on
the same bytes: mcp-recall's real hook, the head cut to the same size,
the first line alone, and pass-through. It scores the facts each keeps
(paths, changed lines, commits, error lines, merge state) and the false
claims each makes. The facts come from rules over the raw output that
import nothing from src/, so a handler bug cannot also be an extractor
bug and score as a pass.

if the first line is not below mcp-recall in every family (the benchmark
could not fail). bun test fails when benchmark/results.md is stale, so a
change's effect on quality shows in its PR diff.

depend on the installed git. scripts/quality-corpus.ts rebuilds it with
pinned authors, dates and config.

* fix: keep the changed lines git diff summaries dropped (#389)

A diff over 8 KB was summarized as per-file +/- counts, so the lines Claude
went on to quote were gone: 5 of 49 referenced added lines survived, and
compressed git diff recall (31.5%) sat below a same-size head (33.1%).

The summary now delivers up to 4 KB of hunks, shared fairly across files so
one large file cannot crowd out the rest, drops index and ---/+++ lines,
keeps git show's commit header, and names what was cut per file. The
per-file list appears only when something was cut, and a file whose share
holds no hunk line is left to it, so a many-file diff costs no more than
before plus the budget.

bun run fidelity: git diff 61.8% vs head 60.2% (from 31.5% vs 33.1%);
all compressed 54.4% vs 53.0% (from 48.2% vs 47.5%). Reduction on the
family 30.2% from 37.5%. 2 KB and 8 KB budgets both fell below head.

* fix: skip --binary patch data and mark a cut commit header

Review on #394: a GIT binary patch body fell through to a headerless hunk,
so its encoded data reached the summary and its +/- characters were counted
as changed lines. And a commit header past 20 lines was cut with no marker,
